title: Spiritual Tourism in Odisha: Puri, Bhubaneswar and Konark
seoTitle: Spiritual Places in Odisha: Puri, Bhubaneswar & Konark | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Plan a spiritual trip in Odisha: the Jagannath Temple and Rath Yatra in Puri, Bhubaneswar's temples, Konark, the Jain caves and the Buddhist Diamond Triangle.
description: A guide to spiritual tourism in Odisha: the Jagannath Temple in Puri and its Rath Yatra and Mahaprasad, Bhubaneswar's Lingaraj and old temples, the Sun Temple at Konark, the Jain caves of Udayagiri and Khandagiri, Dhauli, the Buddhist sites of Ratnagiri, Udayagiri and Lalitgiri, Devi shrines such as Biraja and Tara Tarini, entry rules and a golden triangle route.
dek: Odisha's golden triangle of Puri, Bhubaneswar and Konark holds one of the four dhams, a city of temples and a UNESCO sun temple.

hero.alt: Spires of the Lingaraj Temple complex in Bhubaneswar, Odisha

intro: Puri's Jagannath Temple, one of the four dhams of India, is the heart of Odisha's religious life, and its annual Rath Yatra is one of the country's great festivals. An hour away, Bhubaneswar is known as a city of temples, with the Lingaraj and dozens of older shrines in the Kalinga style, and the Sun Temple at Konark is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Odisha also has important Jain and Buddhist heritage: the rock-cut caves of Udayagiri and Khandagiri, the Shanti Stupa at Dhauli near the site of the Kalinga war, and the monastic ruins of Ratnagiri, Udayagiri and Lalitgiri.
quickAnswer: Odisha's main spiritual destinations are the Jagannath Temple in Puri (which admits only Hindus) with its Rath Yatra in June or July, the Lingaraj and other temples of Bhubaneswar, the Sun Temple at Konark, the Jain caves of Udayagiri and Khandagiri, Dhauli, and the Buddhist sites of Ratnagiri, Udayagiri and Lalitgiri. Puri, Konark and Bhubaneswar are within about 65 km of each other. October to March is the best time.
takeaways: Puri, Bhubaneswar and Konark form a golden triangle within about 65 km of each other.
The Jagannath Temple and Lingaraj admit only Hindus; Lingaraj has a viewing platform outside.
The Rath Yatra falls in June or July each year.
Konark's Sun Temple is a UNESCO site and a monument, not an active temple.
Ratnagiri, Udayagiri and Lalitgiri are major Buddhist sites north of Bhubaneswar.

items.name: Puri
body: The Jagannath Temple, built in the 12th century, with its kitchen and Ananda Bazar, where Mahaprasad is sold. Non-Hindus can view the temple from outside.

image.alt: The Jagannath Temple in Puri, Odisha
image.caption: Jagannath Temple, Puri

items.name: Bhubaneswar
body: The 11th-century Lingaraj and a trail of older temples, including Mukteswar and Rajarani.

items.name: Konark
body: The Sun Temple, carved as a chariot with stone wheels, built in the 13th century.

items.name: Rath Yatra
body: Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra ride on three chariots from the temple to the Gundicha temple in Ashadha (June or July).

sections.heading: More sacred places
list: Sakshi Gopal, a Krishna temple between Bhubaneswar and Puri.
The Kalijai temple on an island in Chilika lake.
Biraja at Jajpur and Tara Tarini near Berhampur, both revered Devi shrines.
Ratnagiri, Udayagiri and Lalitgiri, about 100 km north-east of Bhubaneswar.

rows: Puri during the festival (book months ahead)

sections.heading: Stays and tips
list: Puri has hotels along the sea front and near the temple; book very early for the Rath Yatra.
Bhubaneswar has the widest choice and is the best base for the temples and Buddhist sites.
Mobile phones, cameras and leather items are not allowed inside the Jagannath Temple; use the lockers.
The Mahaprasad from the temple kitchen is available in the Ananda Bazar inside the complex.

sections.heading: Festivals
list: Rath Yatra (June or July) in Puri, followed nine days later by the return journey (Bahuda Yatra).
Snana Purnima, the ritual bathing of the deities about two weeks before the Rath Yatra.
Maha Shivratri at the Lingaraj temple.
The Konark Dance Festival in December, held against the Sun Temple.

safety: Darshan waits vary from minutes to many hours; no one can guarantee quick darshan, so plan buffer time.
Dress modestly and follow each place of worship's rules on dress, phones and photography.
The Rath Yatra crowds are immense; follow police arrangements and stay with your group.
The sea at Puri has strong currents; swim only where lifeguards are present.
packing: ID and hotel bookings for festival dates

faqs.q: Can non-Hindus enter the Jagannath Temple in Puri?
faqs.a: No. The temple admits only Hindus; others can view it from outside.

faqs.q: When is the Rath Yatra in Puri?
faqs.a: In the month of Ashadha, usually June or July; check the year's date.

faqs.q: How far is Konark from Puri?
Is the Konark Sun Temple an active temple?
faqs.a: No. It is a protected monument and UNESCO World Heritage Site.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Puri, Konark and Bhubaneswar?
faqs.a: Three to four days covers the main temples comfortably.
Food offered to Jagannath and sold at the Ananda Bazar inside the temple complex.
